review.summary: The commit makes URI parsing and the URI keyword constructor reject syntactically invalid authority components (userinfo, host, port) and raw ASCII whitespace/control characters, replacing the narrow CR/LF-only check. This fixes concrete defects tracked in issues #25 (malformed host '127.0.0.1 @test.com' accepted, causing requests to reach an unintended host) and #45 (non-decimal port '//foo.com:bar' accepted despite RFC 3986 port = *DIGIT). The added helpers are internal (underscore-prefixed) and no public API surface is extended.
review.evidence: Production patch narrows accepted characters via _is_forbidden_ascii and adds _is_valid_userinfo/_is_valid_host plus digit-only port checks in both URI(uri::URI; ...) and parse_uri_reference, so previously-accepted malformed URIs now throw ArgumentError/ParseError. Issue #74 explicitly states it closes #25 and #45, matching the commit content. Test patch adds testsets 'Forbidden ASCII Characters' and 'Invalid Authorities' asserting rejection of 'http://foo@127.0.0.1 @test.com:8080/test', '//foo.com:bar', 'http://example.com:80a/', percent-escape errors like 'a%GG', and confirming valid cases still parse (a%40b userinfo, fe80::a%25eth0 IP literal, empty port). Runtime evidence reports stable_differential over 3 repetitions with the fixed full suite passing. Minimization kept all 4 hunks and is reported globally minimal.

review.validation_risks: The fix tightens accepted input, so it changes existing behavior for URIs containing raw spaces, tabs, form feeds, DEL, and malformed authorities; existing expectations in test/uri.jl had to be flipped (tab/form-feed URLs, unencoded IPv6 zone ID), which means the trigger test file diverges from the parent revision's expectations in places beyond the new testsets. Reproduction must therefore apply the full upstream test patch, not just the added testsets. The dedicated trigger script also includes a network-dependent 'download' testset hitting httpbingo.julialang.org, which can fail for reasons unrelated to the defect; scope execution to the two named testsets to avoid flakiness. Unicode host handling is deliberately left permissive (tracked separately as #41), so do not treat Unicode cases as part of this defect.
review.suggested_tests: Run only the 'Invalid Authorities' and 'Forbidden ASCII Characters' testsets against parent and fixed revisions. Key assertions: @test_throws URIs.ParseError URI("http://foo@127.0.0.1 @test.com:8080/test"); @test_throws URIs.ParseError URI("//foo.com:bar"); @test_throws URIs.ParseError URI("http://example.com:80a/"); @test_throws URIs.ParseError URI("http://a%GG@hostname/"); @test_throws ArgumentError URI(; scheme="http", host="foo@bar"); @test_throws ArgumentError URI(; scheme="http", host="foo.com", port="bar"). Negative-control assertions to guard against over-rejection: URI("http://a%40b@foo%41.com/").host == "foo%41.com"; URI("http://[fe80::a%25eth0]/").host == "fe80::a%25eth0"; URI("//foo.com:").port == "".
